name: Authentication Events
purpose: Identifies where authentication of credentials actually occurred, distinguishing local/workgroup account authentication (recorded on the workstation itself) from domain/Active Directory authentication (recorded on the domain controller), via NTLM and Kerberos protocol events.
key_fields: Event ID 4776 (NTLM) - the system attempted to validate credentials for an account, success or failure
Event ID 4768 (Kerberos) - a Ticket Granting Ticket was requested/granted, indicating a successful logon
Event ID 4769 (Kerberos) - a Service Ticket was requested, indicating access to a server resource
Event ID 4771 (Kerberos) - Kerberos pre-authentication failed, indicating a failed logon
normal_baseline: 4768/4769 activity concentrated on domain controllers, matching normal business-hours logon and resource-access patterns for known accounts; 4776 activity limited to expected local/workgroup authentication scenarios.
anomalies: A burst of 4771 (Kerberos pre-authentication failed) events against one or many accounts followed by a 4768 success, consistent with a password-spray or brute-force attack that ultimately succeeded
4769 Service Ticket requests for service accounts using weak/legacy ticket encryption at unusual hours, consistent with Kerberoasting
4776 NTLM authentication occurring where Kerberos would normally be expected for that account/resource, consistent with a forced protocol downgrade or a pass-the-hash style attempt

Authentication events recorded on a host other than where the analyst expects for that account type (e.g., a domain account appearing to authenticate locally rather than at a domain controller), consistent with cached-credential logon
anti_forensic_notes: These events are recorded only on the system that actually performed the authentication - a host showing no local 4776/4768/4769 activity for a given account has not necessarily seen no authentication, it may simply mean the authentication happened elsewhere (the domain controller for a domain account). Standard Security-log clearing and retention limits otherwise apply (see security-eventlog's Event ID 1102 note).
interpretation: Authentication events identify where authentication of credentials occurred, which is particularly useful when tracking local vs. domain account usage. They are recorded on the system that authenticated the credentials: Local Account/Workgroup authentication is recorded on the workstation itself, while Domain/Active Directory authentication is recorded on the domain controller.
